new.title: A batch of two-name calibrations can retain exactly one measured bit per raw key bit
new.unlocks: retains the full calibration in exactly nk binary measurements across n independent keys
new.context: The reply difference is affine. Select independent coordinate rows and call its kernel T. The mixer kernel K has index two in T. Choose a lift t in T outside K. Add s-1 parities distinguishing points of the kernel. This resolves each difference fiber. Repeat per key. A smaller budget cannot exist because a batch fiber has 2^(ns) keys. new.title: Some pair of fixed row names identifies every raw key exactly at widths other than one and three
new.statement:
∀ (k : Nat) (hk : 0 < k),
  let W := Fin k → Bool
  let ix := fun (i : Nat) => (⟨i % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let add := fun (u v : W) (i : Fin k) => xor (u i) (v i)
  let mix := fun (d : Nat) (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    xor (x (ix (i.val+k-d % k))) (xor (x i) (x (ix (i.val+d))))
  let rot := fun (a : Nat) (x : W) (i : Fin k) => x (ix (i.val+k-a % k))
  let chi := fun (r : W) (i : Fin k) => xor (r i) (!(r (ix (i.val+1))) && r (ix (i.val+2)))
  let row := fun (name x : W) => add (chi (mix 1 (add name (rot 1 x)))) x
  let m := 1 + (k-1) % 3
  (∀ q : Nat, (∃ names : Fin q → W, Function.Injective (fun x : W => fun j : Fin q => row (names j) x)) ↔
    k ≠ 1 ∧ k ≠ 3 ∧ 2 ≤ q) ∧
  ((k = 2 ∨ 4 ≤ k) → ∃ v : W,
    (∀ i : Fin k, mix 1 v i = (if k = 2 then decide (i.val = 1) else decide (m ≤ i.val))) ∧
    ∀ u : W, Function.Injective (fun x : W => (row u x, row (add u v) x)))
new.unlocks: identifies the entire unknown raw key using a suitable fixed pair of row names even at singular mixer widths
new.context: Let N be the mixed name difference. A collision forces the mixed key difference B to be constant on the run of ones and zero at adjacent zeros. For three zeros the residue sums force the middle bit of B to vanish. The only nonzero possibility is N. Then the baseline fixes the raw difference. With one or two zeros its boundary bits contradict the cyclic recurrence. With three zeros the baseline forces unequal residue sums of the mixed key. A one-name calibration cannot exist because the cancelling key and its complement collide. Allow 120 to 210 minutes.

new.title: The independence number of marked endpoints determines the NOT budget for vertex cover with parity outputs
new.statement:
∀ n : Nat, ∀ G H : Finset (Fin n × Fin n),
  (∀ e ∈ G, e.1 < e.2) → H ⊆ G →
  let active := H.image Prod.fst ∪ H.image Prod.snd
  let independent := fun S : Finset (Fin n) =>
    S ⊆ active ∧ ∀ e ∈ G, ¬(e.1 ∈ S ∧ e.2 ∈ S)
  let cover := fun x : Fin n → Bool => ∀ e ∈ G, x e.1=true ∨ x e.2=true
  ∀ r : Nat,
    (∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit)
        (tap : ↥H → Fin (n+2+C.size)),
      PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n+2) C ∧
      C.output < n+2+C.size ∧ PEqualNP.NotBracket.notCount C ≤ r ∧
      ∀ x : Fin n → Bool,
        let inputs := List.ofFn x ++ [false,true]
        (C.eval inputs = true ↔ cover x) ∧
        (cover x → ∀ e, (C.wires inputs).getD (tap e).val false = xor (x e.val.1) (x e.val.2))) ↔
    ∀ S : Finset (Fin n), independent S → S.card < 2^r
new.unlocks: Gives a common inversion budget for all marked-edge witness circuits while leaving their total gate costs open.
new.context: Fill the zero vertices of an independent set one at a time. At every step some marked edge loses its parity signal. A circuit with r negations has at most two to the power r minus one downward steps on an increasing chain. For the construction, give each cover the rank alpha minus its number of zeros among marked endpoints. Read the rank bits from high to low. On covers augmented by earlier bits and their complements, the next bit has a monotone extension. Negate it once. At equal rank comparable covers agree on every marked endpoint, so each parity has a monotone extension.

changed.title: Exact shared gate count for arbitrarily correlated regular binary block pencils with independent top outputs
changed.statement:
let nonlinear := fun (g : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) =>
  (g.inputs.length == 2) &&
  xor (xor (g.op.eval [false, false]) (g.op.eval [false, true]))
      (xor (g.op.eval [true, false]) (g.op.eval [true, true]))
let depths := fun (width : ℕ) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
  C.gates.foldl (fun (ds : List ℕ) g =>
    ds ++ [(g.inputs.map (fun a => ds.getD a 0)).foldr max 0 + (nonlinear g).toNat])
    (List.replicate width 0)
let F := ZMod 2
∀ (l : ℕ) (d : Fin l → ℕ),
  let I := Σ i : Fin l, Fin (2 * d i)
  let T := Matrix I I F
  let W := Fin l → Fin 2 → F
  ∀ (U V : (i : Fin l) → Matrix (Fin (2 * d i)) (Fin (2 * d i)) F),
    (∀ i, (U i).rank = 2*d i ∧ (V i).rank = 2*d i ∧
      (U i + V i).rank = 2*d i) →
    ∀ (S : Submodule F T) (Q : Submodule F W),
      S = Submodule.span F {A : T | A ∈ S ∧ A.rank ≤ 2} →
      let dimension := fun i : Fin l =>
        Module.finrank F (Submodule.span F {v : Fin 2 → F | ∃ z ∈ Q, z i = v})
      let cost := Module.finrank F S + ∑ i,
        if dimension i = 0 then 0 else if dimension i = 1 then 2*d i else 3*d i
      let K := fun (z : W) =>
        Matrix.blockDiagonal' (fun i => z i 0 • U i + z i 1 • V i)
      let w := Fintype.card (I ⊕ I)
      let coord := Fintype.equivFin (I ⊕ I)
      let table := fun (A : T) (z : W) (x y : Fin (w+1)) =>
        let X := Matrix.fromBlocks A (K z) (K z).transpose (0 : T)
        Fin.cases false (fun i => Fin.cases false (fun j =>
          decide (X (coord.symm i) (coord.symm j) ≠ 0)) y) x
      ∀ t : ℕ,
        (∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (tap : T → W → ℕ),
          PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack ((w+1)+(w+1)) C ∧
          (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧ C.gates.countP nonlinear ≤ t ∧
          ∀ A ∈ S, ∀ z ∈ Q,
            (depths ((w+1)+(w+1)) C).getD (tap A z) 0 ≤ 1 ∧
            PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (table A z) ⟨C.gates, tap A z⟩) ↔ cost ≤ t

A one-dimensional projection needs 2d reflected rank-one summands. For a full projection use the three-ball theorem at radii d: the center and the two differences each need d rank-one summands. Reflect and embed each in its own block, then XOR at taps.

changed.title: Fixed bank parities can choose a shared key despite e bit flips exactly at binary code lengths for 2n bits
changed.statement:
∀ (h k start n a b e : Nat), 5 ≤ h → h+6 ≤ k →
  let tap := fun (x j back : Nat) => x.testBit ((start+j+k-back) % k)
  let pulse := fun (col : Bool) (x j : Nat) =>
    if col then xor (tap x j 1) (xor (tap x j 3) (tap x j 5))
    else xor (tap x j 0) (xor (tap x j 1) (tap x j 2))
  let chi := fun (bits : Nat → Bool) (j : Nat) =>
    xor (bits j) (!(bits (j+1)) && bits (j+2))
  let fiber := fun (z : Fin h → Bool) =>
    {u : Nat | u < 2^(h+2) ∧ ∀ j : Fin h, chi (fun i => u.testBit i) j = z j}
  let tail := fun (col : Bool) (x len u : Nat) =>
    (Finset.range len).filter (fun j =>
      chi (fun i => xor (u.testBit i) (pulse col x i)) (h-len+j))
  let ok := fun (x : Nat) (r c : Fin h → Bool) =>
    Set.InjOn (tail false x 5) (fiber r) ∧ Set.InjOn (tail true x 4) (fiber c)
  let F := ZMod 2
  let V := Fin n → Fin h → F
  let dist := fun {m : Nat} (x y : Fin m → F) =>
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => x i ≠ y i)).card
  let code := fun (m : Nat) =>
    ∃ E : (Fin (2*n) → F) →ₗ[F] (Fin m → F),
      ∀ u v, u ≠ v → 2*e < dist (E u) (E v)
  (∃ (menu : Fin 3 → Fin (2^k)) (L : V →ₗ[F] (Fin a → F))
     (R : V →ₗ[F] (Fin b → F)) (out : (Fin a → F) → (Fin b → F) → Fin n → Fin 3),
    Function.Injective menu ∧ ∀ (r c : V) (s : Fin a → F) (t : Fin b → F),
      dist (L r) s + dist (R c) t ≤ e →
      ∀ j, ok (menu (out s t j)).val (fun i => decide (r j i ≠ 0))
        (fun i => decide (c j i ≠ 0))) ↔ code a ∧ code b
changed.unlocks: determines both message lengths needed to choose physical keys when some measured bits can flip
changed.context: The last and third-last row bits and last two column bits suffice for the three raw keys. Encode these 2n bits on each bank. Conversely take three rejecting witnesses per bank. Their pairwise differences fill a binary plane, so every vector in its n-fold sum is a difference of hard words. At a changed site let the opposite bank forbid the third key. The two outputs are incompatible. Messages within distance 2e share a corrupted word, a contradiction. A smaller-circuit companion cannot exist because the budget counts transmitted bits. Allow 100 to 180 minutes.

changed.title: Choosing a shared key and decoding both hidden strips costs two nonlinear fan-in-two gates per site to leading order
changed.statement:
let nonlinear := fun (g : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) =>
  (g.inputs.length == 2) &&
    xor (xor (g.op.eval [false,false]) (g.op.eval [false,true]))
        (xor (g.op.eval [true,false]) (g.op.eval [true,true]))
let valid := fun (w : Nat) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack w C ∧
  ∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2
let chi := fun (u : Nat → Bool) (i : Nat) => xor (u i) (!(u (i+1)) && u (i+2))
let feasible := fun (h k start n p d K : Nat) =>
  let U := Fin n → Fin (2^(h+2))
  let w := 2*n*h
  let W := w+n*(k+9)
  let shift := fun (col : Bool) (x j : Nat) =>
    let bit := fun back : Nat => x.testBit ((start+j+k-back) % k)
    if col then xor (bit 1) (xor (bit 3) (bit 5))
    else xor (bit 0) (xor (bit 1) (bit 2))
  let observe := fun (col : Bool) (x u len : Nat) =>
    List.ofFn (fun i : Fin len =>
      chi (fun l => xor (u.testBit l) (shift col x l)) (h-len+i.val))
  ∃ (menu : Finset Nat) (P D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit)
    (keyTap : Fin n → Fin k → Nat) (out : Fin n → Bool → Fin (h+2) → Nat),
    menu ⊆ Finset.range (2^k) ∧ menu.card = 3 ∧ valid w P ∧ valid W D ∧
    (∀ j i, keyTap j i < w+P.gates.length) ∧
    (∀ j col i, out j col i < W+D.gates.length) ∧
    d*(P.gates.countP nonlinear+D.gates.countP nonlinear) ≤ n*(p*h+K) ∧
    ∀ (r c : U),
      let reply := fun (u : Nat) => List.ofFn (fun i : Fin h => chi (fun l => u.testBit l) i)
      let y := (List.ofFn (fun j : Fin n => reply (r j).val ++ reply (c j).val)).flatten
      let pre := P.wires y
      let chosen := fun j : Fin n =>
        ∑ i : Fin k, if pre.getD (keyTap j i) false then 2^i.val else 0
      (∀ j, chosen j ∈ menu) ∧
      let data := (List.ofFn (fun j : Fin n =>
        List.ofFn (fun i : Fin k => (chosen j).testBit i) ++
        observe false (chosen j) (r j).val 5 ++ observe true (chosen j) (c j).val 4)).flatten
      let wires := D.wires (y ++ data)
      ∀ j col i, wires.getD (out j col i) false = (if col then c j else r j).val.testBit i
∀ (p d : Nat), 0 < d →
  ((∃ K : Nat, ∀ (h k start n : Nat), 5 ≤ h → h+6 ≤ k → feasible h k start n p d K) ↔
  2*d ≤ p)

changed.title: Two complementary names leave an exact number of indistinguishable raw key pairs on a cyclic bank
changed.statement:
∀ (k : Nat) (hk : 0 < k) (d ini fin : Nat),
  let W := Fin k → Bool
  let ix := fun (i : Nat) => (⟨i % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (a : Nat) (x : W) (i : Fin k) => x (ix (i.val+k-a % k))
  let mix := fun (gap : Nat) (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    xor (x (ix (i.val+k-gap % k))) (xor (x i) (x (ix (i.val+gap))))
  let chi := fun (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    xor (x i) (!(x (ix (i.val+1))) && x (ix (i.val+2)))
  let view := fun (x : W) (b : Bool) (i : Fin k) =>
    xor (chi (fun t => xor (mix d (rot ini x) t) b) i) (rot fin x i)
  let keys : Finset W := Finset.univ
  let paired := fun x : W => (keys.filter (fun y => view y = view x)).card
  let g := Nat.gcd k (2*d)
  let e := if 3 ∣ k/g then 2*g else 0
  (∀ x, paired x ≤ 2) ∧
  (keys.filter (fun x => paired x = 2)).card = 2 * 2^e ∧
  (keys.image view).card + 2^e = 2^k

changed.title: When signed binary-clause SAT probes identify every possible visible support and how many probes suffice
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : Nat) (u v : Fin m → Fin n), (∀ i, u i ≠ v i) →
  let Bits := Finset (Fin n)
  let cube := (Finset.univ : Finset Bits)
  let labels := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m))
  let cut := fun (S : Bits) => labels.filter
    (fun i => decide (u i ∈ S) != decide (v i ∈ S))
  let components := cube.filter (fun C => C.Nonempty ∧ (cut C).card = 0 ∧
    ∀ D ∈ C.powerset, D.Nonempty → (cut D).card = 0 → D = C)
  let strong := labels.filter (fun i => ∀ S ∈ cube,
    (decide (u i ∈ S) != decide (v i ∈ S)) = true → 3 ≤ (cut S).card)
  let good := fun (C : Bits) => strong.toList.any (fun i => decide (u i ∈ C))
  let Signing := Fin m → Bool × Bool
  let sat := fun (A : Finset Bits) (p : Signing) =>
    ∃ x ∈ A, ∀ i, (decide (u i ∈ x), decide (v i ∈ x)) ≠ p i
  ∀ k : Nat,
    (∃ Q : Finset Signing, Q.card ≤ k ∧
      ∀ A B : Finset Bits, (∀ p ∈ Q, (sat A p ↔ sat B p)) → A = B) ↔
      (∀ C ∈ components, good C = true) ∧ 2 ^ n ≤ k

changed.context: Compare the full cube with each one-word deletion: each word needs its own singleton test. Flip bits to isolate zero. Each clause is an implication or forbids both ends true. A sink strong component of implications must contain a forbidden pair, else turning on that component gives another solution. Every cut separating that pair has an arc each way and the forbidden edge. Conversely remove such an edge. Two edge-disjoint alternate paths exist by Menger; orient them oppositely and feed remaining vertices toward their union. Forbid both ends true. Translate to isolate every word.

changed.title: Sharp adaptive query cost with corrupted SAT replies inside an even parity class of a cycle
changed.statement:
∀ (n k e : Nat),
  let Site := Fin (n + 2)
  let Bits := Finset Site
  let Signing := Site → Bool × Bool
  let vertex := (Finset.univ : Finset Site)
  let reply := fun (A : Finset Bits) (q : Signing) => A.toList.any (fun x =>
    vertex.toList.all (fun i =>
      (decide (i ∈ x), decide ((i + 1 : Site) ∈ x)) != q i))
  ∀ (T : Bits) (D : Finset Bits) (b : Nat), T.Nonempty → Even T.card →
    (∀ x ∈ D, (x ∩ T).card % 2 = b % 2) →
    ( (∃ ask : Fin k → List Bool → Signing, ∃ answer : List Bool → Bool,
        ∀ (A : Finset Bits) (flips : Finset (Fin k)), flips.card ≤ e →
          answer ((List.finRange k).foldl (fun h j => h ++ [reply A (ask j h) != decide (j ∈ flips)])
            ([] : List Bool)) = decide (A ∩ D).Nonempty) ↔
      (∀ x ∈ D, vertex \ x ∈ D) ∧ (D = ∅ ∨ (D.card / 2) * (e + 1) + e ≤ k) )
changed.unlocks: Determine the exact number of adaptive SAT replies needed when some answers can be false.
changed.context: A nonempty probe confined to the parity class is a complementary pair: a directed implication cycle synchronizes all bits. Otherwise at most one bit is forced and each live singleton can toggle between two models. Use the cube outside D as baseline. Along its truthful path every pair needs e+1 distinguishing probes, or its added word can mimic it. Just before the last pair reaches e+1, switch to truthful replies for its added word. For e more steps the baseline can mimic it. Conversely query each pair until e+1 no replies there, accepting as soon as yes replies total e+1.

changed.title: Exact worst-case list recovery of modular linear outputs from adaptively selected batches of readings
changed.statement:
∀ (m n g b h k L s q : Nat), 0 < q → s ≤ q →
  let F := Fin (m + 1)
  let X := Fin n → F
  let Reply := Fin b → Nat
  let Output := Fin h → Nat
  let cube := (Finset.univ : Finset X)
  let bits := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n))
  ∀ (A : Fin g → Fin b → Fin n → F) (B : Fin h → Fin n → F),
  let dot := fun (a : Fin n → F) (x : X) =>
    bits.sum (fun i => (a i).val * (x i).val) % (m + 1)
  let readout := fun (i : Option (Fin g)) (x : X) (j : Fin b) =>
    i.elim 0 (fun a => dot (A a j) x)
  let goal := fun (x : X) (j : Fin h) => dot (B j) x
  let uncertainty := fun (M : Finset (Fin g)) =>
    ((cube.filter (fun x => ∀ a ∈ M, ∀ j : Fin b, dot (A a j) x = 0)).image goal).card
  ( (∃ N : Nat, 0 < N ∧
      ∃ ask : Fin N → Fin k → List Reply → Option (Fin g),
      ∃ out : Fin N → List Reply → Finset Output,
      (∀ c z, (out c z).card ≤ L) ∧ ∀ x : X,
        let wins := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin N)).filter (fun c =>
          goal x ∈ out c ((List.finRange k).foldl (fun hist j =>
            hist ++ [readout (ask c j hist) x]) ([] : List Reply)))
        s * N ≤ q * wins.card) ↔
    ∃ M : Finset (Fin g), M.card ≤ k ∧ s * uncertainty M ≤ q * L )
changed.unlocks: Determine whether adaptively chosen batches improve randomized recovery of a residual count or a list of outputs.
changed.context: Fix a seed and a transcript. Its compatible inputs form a coset of the kernel of the batches visited: induction follows the same decisions on every input giving the recorded replies. Under a uniform unknown, the linear output is uniform on D values, so any L guesses succeed on at most L/D of the leaf. Average over leaves and seeds. Conversely query a fixed optimal menu. On each attained transcript, translate a list of min(L,D) possible outputs by a uniform element of the output kernel image. Each possible output is covered equally often.

changed.title: Optimal pairs of translated signing types and optimal near-complete menus for reconstruction modulo eleven
changed.statement:
∀ r : Nat, 2 ≤ r →
  let Kind := Finset (Fin r)
  let Word := Fin r → Fin 16
  let kinds := (Finset.univ : Finset Kind)
  let cube := (Finset.univ : Finset Word)
  let sites := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin r))
  let pass := fun (e : Kind) (z x : Word) => sites.toList.all (fun j =>
    let w := (z j).val ^^^ (x j).val
    (w &&& 3) != 0 && (w &&& 13) != (if j ∈ e then 1 else 0))
  let zeroRead := fun (d : Word → Fin 11) (q : Kind × Word) =>
    ((cube.filter (fun x => pass q.1 q.2 x)).sum (fun x => (d x).val)) % 11 = 0
  let kernelSize := fun (M : Finset Kind) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Word → Fin 11)).filter (fun d =>
      ∀ q ∈ M.product cube, zeroRead d q)).card
  (∀ M : Finset Kind, M.card = 2 →
    let bound := 11 ^ (16 ^ r - 244 * 15 ^ (r - 2))
    bound ≤ kernelSize M ∧ (kernelSize M = bound ↔
      (∅ : Kind) ∈ M ∧ ∃ e ∈ M, e.card = 2)) ∧
  (∀ U : Finset Kind, 2 ≤ U.card → U.card ≤ r →
    let bound := 11 ^ (6 * U.card)
    bound ≤ kernelSize (kinds \ U) ∧ (kernelSize (kinds \ U) = bound ↔
      ∀ e ∈ U, (sites \ e).card = 1))

changed.context: The aligned, opposed and common frequency counts are 15,10,9. For two types all agreeing blocks should align. At distance d the union is largest when one type is fully aligned, by convexity of the two geometric terms. Maximize 1+(2/3)^d-(3/5)^d by first differences: d=2 uniquely. Each omitted type with j aligned positions loses 6^j private frequencies. Omitting one-aligned types only loses just those. Omitting the fully opposed type plus a neighbor loses nine extra shared frequencies. With no such neighbor each other omission costs at least 36. Convert lost rank to kernel size.

changed.statement:
∀ r : Nat,
  let Kind := Finset (Fin r)
  let Word := Fin r → Fin 16

  let cube := (Finset.univ : Finset Word)
  let sites := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin r))
  let pass := fun (e : Kind) (z x : Word) => sites.toList.all (fun j =>

  let zeroRead := fun (d : Word → Fin 11) (q : Kind × Word) =>
    ((cube.filter (fun x => pass q.1 q.2 x)).sum (fun x => (d x).val)) % 11 = 0

    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Word → Fin 11)).filter (fun d =>

    (∀ U : Finset Kind, U.card = l → 11 ^ loss ≤ kernelSize (kinds \ U)) ∧

  minimumAt (r + 1) (min (15 * r + 1) (6 * r + 144)) ∧

changed.title: Which systems of parity checks can signed binary-clause SAT probes observe on a pseudoforest?
changed.statement:
∀ (n m t : Nat) (u v : Fin m → Fin n) (H : Fin t → Finset (Fin n)),
  (∀ i, u i ≠ v i) →
  let Bits := Finset (Fin n)
  let cube := (Finset.univ : Finset Bits)
  let labels := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m))
  let rows := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin t))
  let cut := fun (S : Bits) => labels.filter
    (fun i => decide (u i ∈ S) != decide (v i ∈ S))
  let comps := cube.filter (fun C => C.Nonempty ∧ (cut C).card = 0 ∧
    ∀ D ∈ C.powerset, D.Nonempty → (cut D).card = 0 → D = C)
  let edges := fun (C : Bits) => labels.filter (fun i => u i ∈ C)
  let bridges := labels.filter (fun i => ∃ U ∈ cube, cut U = {i})
  let cyclic := (labels \ bridges).biUnion (fun i => ({u i, v i} : Bits))
  let marked := rows.biUnion H
  (∀ C ∈ comps, (edges C).card ≤ C.card) →
  let Signing := Fin m → Bool × Bool
  let sat := fun (A : Finset Bits) (p : Signing) =>
    ∃ x ∈ A, ∀ i, (decide (u i ∈ x), decide (v i ∈ x)) ≠ p i
  let same := fun (x z : Bits) =>
    ∀ j : Fin t, (x ∩ H j).card % 2 = (z ∩ H j).card % 2
  (∀ A B : Finset Bits, (∀ p, sat A p ↔ sat B p) →
    ∀ z : Bits, ((∃ x ∈ A, same x z) ↔ ∃ x ∈ B, same x z)) ↔
    ∀ C ∈ comps,
      (((edges C).card = C.card) ∧
        ∀ a ∈ marked ∩ C, ∀ b ∈ marked ∩ C, ∀ U ∈ cube,
          a ∈ U → b ∉ U → (bridges ∩ cut U).Nonempty) ∨
      (∀ j : Fin t, H j ∩ C ⊆ cyclic ∧ Even (H j ∩ C).card)
changed.unlocks: Decide which joint parity residual questions the graph of signed SAT probes can answer.
changed.context: Compare the cube outside a fiber with the full cube. One nonempty test must stay in the fiber. Translates by the parity kernel cover it. Normalize a passing word to zero. For any live strong implication component, its forward closure passes both before and after removing that component. Constant checks thus meet each live component evenly. A directed cycle synchronizes its vertices and bridges force none. Otherwise components are singletons. A forced bit must reach both ends of an exclusion, possible only from one cycle fork and its attached tree. Build either orientation locally.

changed.title: One signed trace counts arbitrary parity reports on equally spaced cyclic sensors
changed.statement:
∀ (k r m q s d : Nat), 4 ≤ r → 2 ≤ q → 0 < s → k = q*s → s ≤ d → d < 2*s →
  let u := d-s
  let rot := fun (h w : Nat) =>
    ((w <<< (h % k)) ||| (w >>> (k - h % k))) % 2^k
  let step := fun (w : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i => acc ||| ((xor (w.testBit i)
      (!(w.testBit ((i+1)%k)) && w.testBit ((i+2)%k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let state := fun (col : Bool) (w name : Nat) (c : Fin r → Fin (2^k)) =>
    let g := if col then 2 else 1
    (List.finRange r).foldl (fun x j =>
      step (x ^^^ rot g x ^^^ rot (k-g) x) ^^^
        rot (if col then 3*(j.val+1)+1 else 2*j.val) w ^^^ (c j).val)
      (rot (if col then 3 else 1) w ^^^ name)
  let reach := fun col : Bool => if col then 7*r-2 else 5*r-3
  let delay := fun col : Bool => if col then 3*r+1 else 2*r-2
  let sign := fun b : Bool => if b then (-1 : ℤ) else 1
  let bits := fun (a x : Nat) => (List.range a).map (fun i => x.testBit i)
  let sched := fun (c : Fin r → Fin (2^k)) =>
    (List.finRange r).flatMap (fun j => bits k (c j).val)
  ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (3*k+2*r*k+q+m*q+m+(k+1)) C ∧
    C.size ≤ 2^44*(k+r+m+5)^16*(2^(s-1+u)+2^(3*u)) ∧
    ∀ (nr nc : Fin (2^k)) (cr cc : Fin r → Fin (2^k)) (off : Fin k) (bank : Fin q → Bool),
      let p := fun i : Fin q => (off.val+i.val*s)%k
      let sensor := fun (i : Fin q) (w : Nat) =>
        (state (bank i) w (if bank i then nc.val else nr.val)
          (if bank i then cc else cr)).testBit ((p i + delay (bank i))%k)
      let valid := ∀ i, reach (bank i) ≤ d
      let K := fun (i : Fin q) (a b : Fin (2^u)) =>
        ∑ z : Fin (2^(s-1)),
          if z.val % 2^u = a.val then
            let h := fun (t : Bool) => sensor i (rot (p i)
              ((z.val <<< 1) ||| (t.toNat <<< s) ||| (b.val <<< (s+1))))
            if h false = h true then (0 : ℤ) else sign (h false)
          else 0
      let D := Matrix.trace ((List.ofFn
        (fun i : Fin q => (K i : Matrix (Fin (2^u)) (Fin (2^u)) ℤ))).prod)
      (valid → ∀ y : Fin q → Bool,
        ((Nat.card {w : Fin (2^k) // ∀ i, sensor i w.val = y i}) : ℤ) =
          (2 : ℤ)^(k-q) + sign ((List.ofFn y).foldl xor false) * D) ∧
      ∀ (A : Fin m → Fin (2^q)) (v : Fin m → Bool) (t : Fin (2^(k+1))),
        let obs := fun (w : Nat) (j : Fin m) => (List.finRange q).foldl
          (fun b i => xor b ((A j).val.testBit i.val && sensor i w)) false
        let hits := Nat.card {w : Fin (2^k) // ∀ j, obs w.val j = v j}
        let masks := (List.finRange m).flatMap (fun j => bits q (A j).val)
        C.eval (bits k nr.val ++ bits k nc.val ++ sched cr ++ sched cc ++ bits k off.val ++
          List.ofFn bank ++ masks ++ List.ofFn v ++ bits (k+1) t.val) =
            decide (valid ∧ t.val ≤ hits)
changed.unlocks: Prices arbitrary overlapping parity tests on a cyclic schedule after the first shared pivot, using a single signed trace of dimension determined by the exterior overlap. For fixed spacing the gate count stays polynomial in the number of sensors and reports.
changed.context: Unroll the final injection. A selected sensor is its pivot xor a tail on its own exterior block, next pivot and first u=d-s bits of the next block. Fix the exterior. Proper nonempty masks cancel by a pivot flip. The full character factors into signed unary differences. Sum exterior words grouped by their low u bits and close the ordered product by a trace. Replay each local pair once. Multiply q width-2^u matrices. Binary elimination on the report masks gives consistency, rank and the two parity-class sizes. Compare the signed total to the threshold.

changed.title: Minimum number of additional binary clause scopes needed for division-free recovery of every witness count
changed.statement:
∀ (n t : Nat) (scope : Fin t → Finset (Fin n)),
  (∀ i, (scope i).Nonempty) → (∀ j : Fin n, ∃ i, j ∈ scope i) →
  let Bits := Finset (Fin n)
  let sites := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n))
  let rows := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin t))
  let closed := fun (J : Finset (Fin t)) => J.toList.all (fun i => rows.toList.all
    (fun h => !(decide (scope i ∩ scope h).Nonempty) || decide (h ∈ J)))
  let components := rows.powerset.filter (fun J => J.Nonempty ∧ closed J = true ∧
    ∀ K ∈ J.powerset, K.Nonempty → closed K = true → K = J)
  let support := fun (J : Finset (Fin t)) => J.biUnion scope
  let trees := components.filter (fun J =>
    J.sum (fun i => (scope i).card) + 1 = J.card + (support J).card)
  let widthGCD := fun (J : Finset (Fin t)) => J.gcd (fun i => (scope i).card)
  let bad := trees.filter (fun J => 1 < widthGCD J)
  let evenBad := bad.filter (fun J => widthGCD J % 2 = 0)
  let canRecover := fun (a : Nat) (bank : Fin a → Bits) =>
    let patterns := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin a → Bits)).filter
      (fun p => ∀ i, p i ⊆ bank i)
    ∀ z : Bits, ∃ c : (Fin a → Bits) → Int, ∀ x : Bits,
      (patterns.filter (fun p => ∀ i, x ∩ bank i ≠ p i)).sum c =
        (if x = z then (1 : Int) else 0)
  ∀ k : Nat,
    (∃ (s : Nat) (extra : Fin s → Bits), s ≤ k ∧ (∀ i, (extra i).card = 2) ∧
      canRecover (t + s) (Fin.addCases scope extra)) ↔
      max evenBad.card ((bad.card + 1) / 2) ≤ k
changed.unlocks: Choose the least number of extra binary clauses that remove every arithmetic obstruction to reconstruction.
changed.context: The exceptional frequency on a tree component has divisor 2^g-1 for its width gcd g. Thus precisely the trees with g>1 need repair. One binary scope within a component creates a cycle. Joining two trees gives gcd(g1,g2,2). Each addition removes at most two bad trees and at most one even bad tree. Pair odd bad trees with even ones first, then pair remaining odds. Repair each remaining unpaired tree by joining two distinct internal bits. These exist since every bad width is at least two. Repeated labelled scopes are allowed.

changed.title: Exact modular ambiguity for omissions in the first three Hamming layers of a translated clause bank
changed.statement:
∀ (r t pairs : Nat) (center : Bool), t ≤ r → pairs ≤ Nat.choose r 2 →
  let Kind := Finset (Fin r)
  let Word := Fin r → Fin 16
  let kinds := (Finset.univ : Finset Kind)
  let cube := (Finset.univ : Finset Word)
  let sites := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin r))
  let pass := fun (e : Kind) (z x : Word) => sites.toList.all (fun j =>
    let w := (z j).val ^^^ (x j).val
    (w &&& 3) != 0 && (w &&& 13) != (if j ∈ e then 1 else 0))
  let zeroRead := fun (d : Word → Fin 11) (q : Kind × Word) =>
    ((cube.filter (fun x => pass q.1 q.2 x)).sum (fun x => (d x).val)) % 11 = 0
  let kernelSize := fun (M : Finset Kind) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Word → Fin 11)).filter (fun d =>
      ∀ q ∈ M.product cube, zeroRead d q)).card

    (decide (sites ∈ U) = center) ∧ (∀ e ∈ U, (sites \ e).card ≤ 2) ∧
    (U.filter (fun e => (sites \ e).card = 1)).card = units ∧
    (U.filter (fun e => (sites \ e).card = 2)).card = pairs

changed.title: Minimum additional binary clause scopes for reconstruction from SAT replies
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : Nat) (u v : Fin m → Fin n), (∀ i, u i ≠ v i) →
  let Bits := Finset (Fin n)
  let cube := (Finset.univ : Finset Bits)
  let labels := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m))
  let cut := fun (S : Bits) => labels.filter
    (fun i => decide (u i ∈ S) != decide (v i ∈ S))
  let components := cube.filter (fun C => C.Nonempty ∧ (cut C).card = 0 ∧
    ∀ D ∈ C.powerset, D.Nonempty → (cut D).card = 0 → D = C)
  let strong := labels.filter (fun i => ∀ S ∈ cube,
    (decide (u i ∈ S) != decide (v i ∈ S)) = true → 3 ≤ (cut S).card)
  let good := fun (C : Bits) => strong.toList.any (fun i => decide (u i ∈ C))
  2 ≤ n →
  let bad := (components.filter (fun C => good C = false)).card
  let forest := components.toList.all (fun C =>
    (labels.filter (fun i => u i ∈ C)).card + 1 == C.card)
  let decodes := fun (h : Nat) (a b : Fin h → Fin n) =>
    let sat := fun (A : Finset Bits) (p : Fin h → Bool × Bool) =>
      ∃ x ∈ A, ∀ i, (decide (a i ∈ x), decide (b i ∈ x)) ≠ p i
    ∀ A B : Finset Bits, (∀ p, (sat A p ↔ sat B p)) → A = B
  ∀ k : Nat,
    (∃ (s : Nat) (left right : Fin s → Fin n), s ≤ k ∧ (∀ j, left j ≠ right j) ∧
      decodes (m+s) (Fin.addCases u left) (Fin.addCases v right)) ↔
      bad + (if forest then 1 else 0) ≤ k
changed.unlocks: Choose the smallest augmentation of a fixed binary clause bank for universal SAT support reconstruction.
changed.context: Exact recovery requires a three-edge-connected endpoint pair belonging to an actual edge in every component. One added scope reduces the deficient count by at most one. A forest on n vertices in b components starts with n-b edges; each final component needs at least two independent cycles, so at least n+1 edges overall. If some component already qualifies, attach each deficient one by a bridge. Otherwise duplicate an edge on a cycle to qualify its component, then attach the others. For a forest join it into a tree and add two copies of one tree edge.

changed.title: A shortest matching extension of an arbitrary prescribed matching with nonzero signed containing count is computable in polynomial time
changed.statement:
let header := fun z : Nat => List.replicate z true ++ [false]
let pairs := fun n : Nat => (List.finRange n).flatMap (fun i =>
  ((List.finRange n).filter (fun j => decide (i < j))).map (fun j => (i,j)))
let fast := fun f : List Bool → List Bool =>
  ∃ M : Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => x) (fun x : List Bool => x) f,
    ∀ i, Finite (M.tm.Γ i)
∃ solve : List Bool → List Bool, fast solve ∧
∀ (n : Nat) (E P : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) (rows : List (Finset (Fin n × Fin n) × Bool)),
  (∀ e ∈ E, e.1 < e.2) →
  let ends := fun e : Fin n × Fin n => ({e.1,e.2} : Finset (Fin n))
  let valid := fun Q : Finset (Fin n × Fin n) => Q ⊆ E ∧
    ∀ e ∈ Q, ∀ f ∈ Q, e ≠ f → Disjoint (ends e) (ends f)
  valid P →
  let signed := fun Q : Finset (Fin n × Fin n) =>
    ((rows.filter (fun t => t.2 && decide (Q ⊆ t.1))).length : Int) -
      ((rows.filter (fun t => !t.2 && decide (Q ⊆ t.1))).length : Int)
  let mask := fun A : Finset (Fin n × Fin n) => (pairs n).map (fun e => decide (e ∈ A))
  let good := fun Q => P ⊆ Q ∧ valid Q ∧ signed Q ≠ 0
  let m := (rows.filter (fun t => decide (P ⊆ t.1))).length
  let x := header n ++ mask E ++ mask P ++ header rows.length ++ rows.flatMap (fun t => t.2 :: mask t.1)
  (m = 0 → solve x = [false]) ∧ (solve x = [false] ↔ ¬ ∃ Q, good Q) ∧
  ((∃ Q, good Q) → ∃ Q, good Q ∧ (∀ S, good S → Q.card ≤ S.card) ∧
    2^((Q \ P).card)*(signed Q).natAbs ≤ m ∧ solve x =
      [true] ++ mask Q ++ [decide (signed Q < 0)] ++
        (List.range (rows.length.log2+1)).map (fun i => (signed Q).natAbs.testBit i))
changed.unlocks: Tests all candidate two-probe interactions in polynomial time by finding an actual nonzero extension, with a bound independent of the prescribed matching size.
changed.context: Retain only observations containing P and delete all endpoints of P. If their signed total is nonzero return P. For a smallest residual witness of positive size r every proper containing count, including that at the empty set, vanishes. Inversion forces all 2^r exact traces to have absolute mass |c|. Scan through floor(log2 m) using signed squared matching moments. At the first positive size, delete any edge whose removal keeps that moment positive. Append P and count the signs directly.

changed.title: A kernel support test characterizes exact partitions by syndrome translates of an independent-set probe
changed.unlocks: Decide when a family of parity-check translates attains the independent-set volume bound with zero overlap.
changed.context: Translate collisions occur precisely when two distinct independent representatives differ by a nonzero kernel word. Their two set differences are disjoint independent parts of its support because independence is downward closed. Conversely, any such partition gives two colliding representatives. Thus the support test is exactly injectivity of the translation map from K times I. With the stated cardinality this is equivalent to every word having exactly one representation.
